requirement:
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence
files and MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of {cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation in `requirements.references.builtin_definitions` has code that carries it out. Each also has a test that runs that code and asserts the outcome.

| Obligation | Code | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Built-ins named `habeas:<name>` exist in every project without a declaration | `BUILTINS`, `builtin()` and `is_builtin_name()` in `src/builtins.rs` | `habeas_none_has_its_approved_text_and_only_permits_fenced_citations` |
| Fixed text, documented in the reference documentation | `Builtin::text` and `quoted_text` read the approved requirement text from the book | The same test asserts the text equals the quote in `md/reference.md` |
| The built-in states which roles may use it | `Builtin.roles` and `requires_justification`; `md/reference.md` says "Only `{cite}` may reference it" | The same test |
| References resolve built-in names alongside project definitions | `opening_fence`, `reference_roles` and `definition_blocks` recognise the name form. `validate_references` and `collect_definitions` handle it. `citation_items` and `missing_function_references` resolve built-ins (a built-in counts only in a form it permits). `AssessmentSources::prepare` supplies built-in text. | `opening_fences_take_a_role_and_one_valid_or_built_in_name`; `fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated` |
| The book renders a built-in reference as an unlinked badge whose hover text is the full text | `reference_badge` and `replace_references` in `src/lib.rs` | `fenced_references_render_their_badge_and_body_and_built_ins_are_unlinked` asserts the `title` attribute holds the escaped full text, no `href="habeas…"` appears, and invalid forms stay literal |
| Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence files | They are never inserted into `definitions`. The orphan check and the missing-evidence loop in `inspect_repository_with_progress` therefore neither demand nor accept `evidence/habeas:none.json`. | `built_ins_have_no_evidence_index_entry_or_status_and_are_validated_in_the_book` asserts a stray `evidence/habeas:none.json` is reported and no "missing evidence for habeas:none" appears |
| Built-ins MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the missing-evidence check | Same mechanism | The same test asserts the status table, the status findings, the book chapter names and the index contain no `habeas:` entries |
| A project definition using a `habeas:` name MUST be reported | `collect_definitions` reports "names beginning with habeas: are reserved". `definition_blocks` recognises the reserved name so it can be reported. | `project_definitions_cannot_use_reserved_built_in_names` |
| A reference in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks its stated form, MUST be reported | `Builtin::check`, called from `validate_references` | The `references.rs` tests assert the wrong-role, non-fenced, empty-justification and unknown-built-in errors, in both source and book. The unit test covers `check` directly. |

The `{impl}` references on the inputs match the code that does these things. I found no unmarked implementing code and no unspecified extra behavior. The extra "no matching built-in definition" error for unknown `habeas:` names falls under resolving built-in names and reporting invalid references.

One point could be read two ways. The quoted text of `habeas:none` says "Cite this only when…" but does not explicitly list the permitted roles. I read "the built-in MUST state which roles may use it" as satisfied by the built-in's own `roles` data and the documentation's "Only `{cite}` may reference it". That reading is equally well supported and I did not treat it as a gap.

text: :::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence
files and MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of {cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
:::{req} coverage

Repository validation MUST check that every requirement defined by a fenced `{req}` directive in a chapter under the configured mdBook source directory has an evidence file named `evidence/<full-requirement-name>.json`, and MUST report each requirement whose evidence file is missing. The full name MUST use the chapter's path-derived namespace followed by the directive name; for example, a directive named `check` in `md/requirements.md` has the full name `requirements.check`.
:::{req} identifiers

Requirement and reference names MUST have nonempty dot-separated segments containing only ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. A `{req}` directive whose full name is invalid, including one whose chapter path gives an invalid namespace, and a role with an invalid name MUST remain literal and MUST NOT define or reference a requirement. For nested chapter paths, a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment MUST be omitted from the requirement namespace.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
